_doc: Absolute floors: a PROPOSED (or re-scanned BLESSED) state crossing one of these is HARD-STOP in the gate and FAIL in the monitor. Never ackable. Floors are about the state itself, not the delta; the delta certificate lives in freeze. Missing or malformed policy = UNEVALUATED for every axis (fail-closed).

vuln._doc: kind=vulnerability only; informational advisories (unsound/unmaintained/notice/yanked) never floor. Shape, not score: CVSS scores are not computed here (4.0 scoring is a lookup table, 3.x a formula). A critical SHAPE is network-reachable, no privileges, no user interaction, High impact on one of the listed axes. A (availability) is deliberately excluded by default: a remote DoS in a CI tool is a RAISE to ack, not a floor.

mal._doc: Per-engine acks exist for heuristic/ML false positives; a panel with this many malicious verdicts, or any sandbox behavioural verdict of malicious, is not a false-positive profile. min_verdict_engines is a COMPLETENESS precondition, not a floor (#347 step 1): a panel where fewer engines returned a verdict (malicious+suspicious+undetected+harmless) is still running or a partial rescan, so the record is UNEVALUATED in the gate and FAILS the monitor, never read as clean. Basis: the fleet's complete panels measured 63-71 engines (ELF low, PE high) against VirusTotal's ~70 integrated engines; 50 sits well under a complete panel and well over a half-run one.

caps._doc: Applies only to a MEASURED head inventory with a prior blessed inventory to compare against (a COPIED FORWARD record is not a measurement; a new tool has no prior). Test-scope grants are ignored (they do not ship). A package newly granted one of these classes in runtime or build scope is HARD-STOP.

build_instructions._doc: Build-script directives (#382), evaluated on MEASURED head inventories only: Bubblewrap-mode cackle records a build script's `cargo:` lines under build.allow_build_instructions (#381), except four prefixes it always permits and never records: cargo:rustc-cfg=, cargo:rustc-check-cfg=, cargo:rerun-if-, cargo:warning (cackle src/build_script_checker.rs ALWAYS_PERMITTED at the pinned rev). rustc-env is recorded and its relative rule applies. Cargo's build record (evidence build.jsonl: build-script-executed cfgs and env, as emitted for the binary's own target) carries both; the relative rustc-env rule applies to it against the prior blessed digest's record. Absolute, no prior needed: rustc-link-arg* / rustc-cdylib-link-arg* and any rustc-flags token other than -l/-L (arbitrary linker flags); a rustc-link-search path (or rustc-flags -L) outside the emitting package's own OUT_DIR (<target>/build/<pkg>-<hash>/out or <target>/build/<pkg>/<hash>/out) or its own registry source (<registry>/src/<index>/<pkg>-<version>/); a rustc-* directive this evaluator cannot classify (unknown is never clean). Relative to the prior blessed inventory for the same package: a rustc-env it did not carry. A new rustc-cfg is not a floor: build scripts set cfgs by probing the compiler, so toolchain bumps change them; the gate's build axis raises each one for a build ack bound to the record's bytes. Everything else — a new dynamic rustc-link-lib, system_libs=, even a new self-named static lib — is an inventory ADDITION that the subset rule refuses and an ack must cover: there is deliberately no auto-ALLOW. Links metadata (cargo:include=, root=, conf=, ...) is data for dependents, not an instruction to rustc. Path matching reads only the shape after /build/ or /registry/src/, so it is stable across runners.
